title: MLOps & Machine Learning Systems
description: MLOps concepts: Model registry, CI/CD, data drift, tracking, containerization, and monitoring.

questions.question: Which open-source platform is widely used for tracking experiments, packaging code, and sharing models in MLOps?
questions.explanation: MLflow is an open-source platform for managing the end-to-end machine learning lifecycle, including experiment tracking and model registry.

questions.question: Data Drift refers to changes in the statistical properties of input data over time, while Concept Drift refers to changes in the relationship between input features and target labels.
questions.explanation: True! Data drift (covariate shift) is a change in feature distribution P(X). Concept drift is a change in the mapping P(Y|X).

questions.question: What common MLOps component serves as a centralized repository to store, discover, and serve consistent feature values for both training and online inference?
questions.code:
// Examples: Feast, Hopsworks, Tecton
// Term: ___ store
questions.explanation: A Feature Store provides a unified interface to calculate, store, and serve features to models during training and low-latency inference.

questions.question: Which deployment strategy routes a small percentage (e.g. 5%) of live traffic to the new model version before rolling it out to 100% of users?
questions.explanation: Canary deployment exposes a subset of production traffic to the new candidate model to detect bugs and performance degradation safely.

questions.question: In shadow deployment, the new model receives live production queries and serves its predictions directly back to the end user.
questions.explanation: False! In shadow deployment, the new model processes traffic asynchronously alongside the current model, but its outputs are logged for evaluation and never returned to the user.

questions.question: What is the name of the open-source version control system specifically designed for tracking large datasets and ML models alongside Git?
questions.explanation: DVC (Data Version Control) tracks large data files and model checkpoints using Git-like workflows connected to cloud storage.

questions.question: Which technique reduces model precision from 32-bit floating point (FP32) to 8-bit integers (INT8) to accelerate inference latency and reduce RAM usage?
questions.explanation: Quantization converts high-precision model weights/activations to lower-bit representations (e.g., FP32 to INT8), drastically improving inference throughput.

questions.question: Model Explainability techniques like SHAP and LIME are post-hoc methods used to interpret black-box model predictions.
questions.code:
import shap
explainer = shap.TreeExplainer(model)
shap_values = explainer.shap_values(X)
questions.explanation: True! SHAP (Shapley Additive exPlanations) and LIME provide model-agnostic feature attributions to explain individual predictions.

questions.question: What workflow orchestration tool developed by Apache is commonly used to schedule DAGs (Directed Acyclic Graphs) for ML data pipelines?
questions.code:
from ___ import DAG
from ___.operators.python import PythonOperator
questions.explanation: Apache Airflow allows engineering teams to author, schedule, and monitor complex data and ML training workflows as DAGs in Python.

questions.question: What is the primary risk addressed by logging and tracking both training code commits, dataset hashes, and hyperparameters in MLOps?
questions.explanation: Logging code, data lineage, and hyperparameters ensures strict reproducibility of models across environments and teams.
